Open Qimera Launcher Widget from the dropdown menu next to the Qimera icon. Sign in to Qimera before you start creating your first scene. Remember to use your authorized account for your server. You should see the Qimera Launcher with your account signed in. If you see an error instead contact Qimera.

Qimera is an Unreal Engine platform that unifies real‑time virtual production, augmented reality (AR), and broadcast graphics in a single, operator‑friendly interface. Designed for live environments—from compact green‑screen studios to large‑scale LED XR stages—Qimera keeps physical cameras and virtual worlds perfectly in sync, frame‑accurate, and ready for air.

All‑in‑one workflow – Build virtual sets, AR graphics, data‑driven overlays, and full XR scenes without leaving the Qimera editor. Unreal Engine power – Leverage the latest UE rendering features (Nanite, Lumen, nDisplay, DLSS 4 and more) for photoreal visuals. Template‑based design – Re‑use, adapt, and automate graphics packages through a flexible template system. Multi‑channel output – Drive video walls, keyed green‑screen composites, in‑studio AR, and overlay graphics simultaneously. Integrated camera tracking – Out‑of‑the‑box support for Mo‑Sys, Stype, Ncam, and other major tracking solutions. Built‑in switching – A multi‑camera software switcher lets a single operator cut and mix live feeds directly inside Qimera. Scalable & modular – Add input modules (data feeds, DMX, OSC) and output nodes (SDI, NDI) as your production grows.

Click to composition tab and choose a scene type to create your first scene. Trackless scenes are used for animating and moving the camera inside Qimera. Tracked scenes are used for creating a scene with camera tracking information. You can manage your scenes and virtual camera selection from this menu. Congratulations! You have created your first scene in Qimera. You can now start reading the rest of the documentation to learn more about Qimera's features and capabilities.

Choose a map to launch Qimera. You can select a map from the list or use the search bar to find a specific map. Choose the composition type you want to run this server with. You can use the Qimera Launcher button to launch Qimera with the selected map and composition type. You should see Qimera Interface running with the selected map and composition type.

Create a Markdown file at docs/hello.md: docs/hello.md # Hello This is my **first Docusaurus document**! A new document is now available at http://localhost:3000/docs/hello.

Docusaurus automatically creates a sidebar from the docs folder. Add metadata to customize the sidebar label and position: docs/hello.md --- sidebar_label: 'Hi!' sidebar_position: 3 --- # Hello This is my **first Docusaurus document**! It is also possible to create your sidebar explicitly in sidebars.js: sidebars.js export default { tutorialSidebar: [ 'intro', 'hello', { type: 'category', label: 'Tutorial', items: ['tutorial-basics/create-a-document'], }, ], };

Docusaurus supports Markdown and a few additional features.

Markdown documents have metadata at the top called Front Matter: my-doc.md --- id: my-doc-id title: My document title description: My document description slug: /my-custom-url --- ## Markdown heading Markdown text with [links](./hello.md)
Regular Markdown links are supported, using url paths or relative file paths.

Regular Markdown images are supported. You can use absolute paths to reference images in the static directory (static/img/docusaurus.png): ![Docusaurus logo](/img/docusaurus.png) You can reference images relative to the current file as well. This is particularly useful to colocate images close to the Markdown files using them: ![Docusaurus logo](./img/docusaurus.png)

Markdown code blocks are supported with Syntax highlighting. ```jsx title="src/components/HelloDocusaurus.js" function HelloDocusaurus() { return

Hello, Docusaurus!

; } ``` src/components/HelloDocusaurus.js function HelloDocusaurus() { return

Hello, Docusaurus!

; }

Made by Qimera Corp with Scribe​ 1. Go to windows home button 2. Type "Black Magic Media Express" 3. Click "Log and Capture" 4. Click "Device" 5. Click "Select Input" in this case we going to check SDI 1 6. Click "Check format and framerate" 7. Click "Close Media Express" Tip: Tip! Make sure you close Media Express before opening Qimera Project. The Blackmagic card only works with one software at a time. 8. Double-click "Open Qimera Project" 9. Click "Extend tool bar" 10. Middle-click "Media Profile" 11. Middle-click "Select Media Profile" 12. Click "Launch Qimera" 13. Middle-click "Click on Qimera UI and Press F11 to switch fullscreen mode" 14. Click "Go to I/O module" 15. Click "SDI Configuration" 16. Click "Open Qimera source-01" 17. Click "Blackmagick Media Source" 18. Click "Open Blackmagick Panel" 19. Click "Open panel" 20. Click "Uncheck Auto" 21. Click "Select for this case SDI 1" 22. Click "Select Resolution in this case 1080HD as we saw in the media express software" 23. Click "Select Progressive for this example" 24. Click "29.97" 25. Click "Apply" 26. Click "Open Video Tab" 27. Click "Select in Color Format 10bits" 28. Click "Select sRGB in Override Source Encoding field" 29. Uncheck Just in time Rendering" 30. Click "Play" 31. Red line means the video is on air 32. Click "preview" 33. now you can see the SDI 1 running 34. Save SDI configuration 35. Click "Close panel" 36. SDI 1 Running Made with Scribe​
